A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, algorithms, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original worst-case privacy-auditing simulations and experiments on CIFAR10, Purchase100 and SST-2, including appendix utility and sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original privacy-auditing experiments, simulations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–5 and scenarios S1–S5 retain the same auditing procedures and canary constructions. The added discussion and computational-cost table do not modify the methods.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate crafted worst-case datasets, CIFAR10 fine-tuning, Purchase100 training from scratch and SST-2 text classification. The new label-DP discussion introduces no evaluated task or scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same canary variants, add/remove and substitute accountants, and group-privacy bound where used. Newly cited auditing and label-DP methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Table A1 retain the sample counts, models, optimizers, hyperparameters and evaluation procedures. Figure 3's added DP-Adam statement repeats a setting already documented in v1.

E4.justification: The run-count analysis in Figure 4 and the utility, hyperparameter-sensitivity and privacy-ratio analyses in Figures A1–A5 are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same seed information, auditing runs and repeats, Clopper–Pearson procedure with significance level 0.05, and reporting of two standard errors where used.

E6.justification: Figures 1–4 and A1–A6 retain identical plotted content and findings. The added main-text statement about unchanged model utility repeats evidence already reported in v1's Appendix A.1.

T1.justification: New Table A2 states asymptotic computational-cost bounds for canary construction, repeated training and score processing. The DP definitions, mixture derivation and Theorems 4.1 and 5.1 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and central conclusions retain the same claims about substitute-adjacency auditing and the limitations of add/remove accounting for attribute privacy.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly explains how mislabeled-canary auditing relates to label DP and identifies specialized label-DP mechanisms outside the techniques' applicability. v1 stated only the broader limitation concerning differently operating DP mechanisms.

D1.justification: Table A2 newly documents computational requirements for each auditing phase. Existing implementation settings and code-access information are retained; the new Reproducibility Statement relocates the existing repository disclosure.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 substantially expands auditing-related research context and distinguishes white-box, hidden-state and black-box work. Section 7 additionally positions the approach against specialized label-DP literature, extending v1's scattered auditing references.

P1.justification: v2 adds a related-work subsection and reproducibility, ethics and LLM-use statements, updates author/header formatting, and makes localized wording and cross-reference edits. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table A2, adjusts table and figure placement, reformats the author block, and refines several captions. Existing plots, axes and legends are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Section 2.3 improves research context, Section 7 makes applicability limits more specific, and Table A2 helps readers assess computational requirements. These additions provide a limited improvement in clarity and practical assessment while preserving the original methods and empirical evidence.
